parts.name: eardrum
parts.hint: The thin, tight skin at the end of the canal that shakes when sound hits it — the tympanic membrane.

parts.name: malleus
parts.hint: The hammer — the first of the three tiny bones, joined to the eardrum.

parts.name: incus
parts.hint: The anvil — the middle one of the three tiny bones.

parts.name: stapes
parts.hint: The stirrup — the smallest bone in the body, pressing on the inner ear.

parts.name: vestibule
parts.hint: The small chamber that joins the balance loops to the coiled tube.

parts.name: semicircular canals
parts.hint: Three looping tubes of fluid that sense balance and turning.

parts.name: cochlea
parts.hint: The coiled, snail-shaped tube that turns vibrations into nerve signals.

parts.name: auditory nerve
parts.hint: The bundle that carries hearing and balance messages to the brain.

parts.name: middle ear
parts.hint: The air-filled space behind the eardrum that holds three tiny bones.

parts.name: Eustachian tube
parts.hint: The passage down to the throat that keeps the air pressure equal on both sides of the eardrum.

parts.name: ear canal
parts.hint: The tube that carries sound in from outside to the eardrum.

parts.name: earlobe
parts.hint: The soft, fleshy bottom of the outer flap — where earrings hang.

parts.name: pinna
parts.hint: The outer flap you can see, which catches sound and funnels it inwards (the auricle).
